reuse.why: Every month-wide action, including the new setLastMonthSpending, goes through the existing isMonthWideCategory predicate and getAverageCategories, reuses extractTagsFromText and getSheetValue, and generalises averageToBudgetAmount instead of adding a sibling.

duplication.why: The rule is centralised, but the category column list and joins (hidden, group_hidden, group notes, template EXISTS) are repeated in getBudgetData, getAverageCategories and a new inline query in setZero that nearly copies getAverageCategories.

placement.why: Rule, SQL fragments and the new action live in budget/actions.ts and the handler is registered in budget/app.ts beside its siblings.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps; the averageToBudgetAmount rename is a reasonable generalisation but touches unrelated call sites.

maintainability.why: One predicate with a named options type makes the rule easy to change; the three parallel SELECTs must be kept in step when a new column is needed.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All month-wide actions call isMonthWideCategory; setZero writes its own category query but still applies the shared predicate.

disguised_duplication.where: setZero's inline SELECT is a visible near-copy of getAverageCategories (LEFT instead of INNER JOIN), not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: isMonthWideCategory keeps one options parameter (includeHidden renamed to includeHiddenCategories with a default); the #fixed and template exclusions are part of its single rule expression, and every month-wide action, including setLastMonthSpending, uses it.
